extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates studying commutative algebra/algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Lecture-note style exposition of a-adic/topological completion, inverse limits, properties of completions (exactness, Noetherianity, Cohen structure), and discrete valuation rings (definitions, characterizations, Serre's conditions). Includes definitions, theorems, lemmas, examples, and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local ring is a domain (Theorem 21.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: A regular local ring A is a domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by induction on dimension r = dim(A): reduce by quotienting by an element of a regular system of parameters, use earlier results that quotients are domains and prime ideals; see (21.21) and (21.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence for quotient regularity (Exercise 21.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a Noetherian local ring of dimension r and x1,...,xs in A with s ≤ r. Set a = ⟨x1,...,xs⟩ and B = A/a. Prove equivalent: (1) A is regular, and there are xs+1,...,xr in A with x1,...,xr a regular sop. (2) B is regular of dimension r−s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exercise relates regularity of A together with extension of a partial regular system of parameters to regularity of the quotient B and vice versa; used in proofs like Theorem 21.22 and Proposition 21.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact sequence relating m/m^2 and n/n^2 (Lemma 21.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: For local ring A with maximal ideal m, ideal a, set n := m/a and k := A/m. There is an exact sequence of k-vector spaces: 0 → (m^2 + a)/m^2 → m/m^2 → n/n^2 → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to relate numbers of generators and to count dimensions of tangent spaces; 'The assertion is very easy to check.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Generators of ideal in regular local ring (Proposition 21.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a regular local ring of dimension r and a an ideal. Set B := A/a and assume B is regular of dimension r−s. Then a is generated by s elements, and any such s elements form part of a regular system of parameters of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Lemma 21.23 to compute dim((m^2 + a)/m^2)=s and previous propositions: if b is the ideal generated by chosen s elements then A/b is regular of dimension r−s and domains arguments imply a=b.

rubrics_metrics.name: a-adic filtration and topology; definition of completion (22.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a filtration M = M0 ⊇ M1 ⊇ ... the open sets are unions of cosets m + Mn; the a-adic filtration/topology is standard when a is an ideal. A sequence is Cauchy if terms eventually differ by elements of any fixed Mn; the completion cM is formed from Cauchy sequences modulo those with limit 0, with canonical map M → cM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructions: closures N̄ = ⋂_n (N + Mn); M is separated iff ⋂ Mn = 0; completion is universal for continuous maps into separated complete filtered modules. Examples: polynomial→power-series and p-adic integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion examples (power series and p-adics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: For R = k[X1,...,Xr] and a = ⟨X1,...,Xr⟩, the completion bR is k[[X1,...,Xr]]; for a prime p and a=⟨p⟩, the completion of Z is the p-adic integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete examples illustrate the Cauchy-sequence description and the inverse-limit description of completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: ba ⊆ rad( bR ) (Proposition 22.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring R and ideal a, the extension ba of a in the completion bR satisfies ba ⊆ rad(bR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses geometric series in the complete ring: for x in ba, 1/(1−x) = 1 + x + x^2 + ... in bR, so 1−x is a unit; hence x is in the Jacobson radical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity/separatedness equivalences for completion (Exercise 22.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For R, ideal a, and module M, the following are equivalent: (1) canonical map M → cM is injective; (2) ⋂_n a^n M = {0}; (3) M is separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use definitions of separated (Hausdorff) in the a-adic topology and properties of Cauchy sequences; this gives a test for whether completion embeds the module.

rubrics_metrics.name: M injects into cM for finitely generated modules under adic hypotheses (Corollary 22.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Noetherian, a ⊆ rad(R), and M is finitely generated, then the canonical map M → cM is injective (i.e., M ⊆ cM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from (22.4) together with Krull Intersection Theorem / Artin–Rees as referenced (18.28 or 20.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse limit construction and universal mapping property (22.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inverse limit lim← Qn is the submodule of Π Qn of compatible tuples (qn) with transition maps Qn+1 → Qn; it has the usual UMP and yields isomorphisms lim← Hom(P, Qn) ≅ Hom(P, lim← Qn) and lim← Hom(Qn, N) ≅ Hom(lim← Qn, N).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also: exactness behavior—given short exact sequences of inverse systems, 0 → lim← Q′_n → lim← Q_n → lim← Q''_n → 0 is exact and the last map is surjective if the transition maps in Q′ system are surjective (Mittag–Leffler type condition). Snake Lemma/diagram chase used in proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion equals inverse limit of quotients (Proposition 22.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a filtered module M = M0 ⊇ M1 ⊇ ..., the completion cM is (canonically) isomorphic to lim← (M/Mn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map constructed by sending a Cauchy sequence to its eventual residues qn in M/Mn; surjectivity obtained by choosing representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of local ring is local (Proposition 22.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a ring with maximal ideal m then its completion bA is a local ring with maximal ideal bm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: bA/bm = A/m, rad(bA) ⊆ bm by (22.2), and any maximal ideal of bA contains rad(bA) hence equals bm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units in completion and relation to localization (22.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given canonical map R → bR, the image of t ∈ R is a unit in bR iff each residue tn ∈ R/a^n is a unit. Define T = preimage in R of units of bR (equivalently elements lying in no maximal ideal containing a). Then S = 1 + a ⊆ T, and bR is the completion of the localization S^{-1}R and, when a is maximal m, of R_m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to relate completion and localization; for Noetherian rings the natural maps from localizations into completions are injective (Krull Intersection / Artin–Rees used).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of completion on finitely generated modules (Theorem 22.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian ring R and ideal a, the functor M ↦ cM (completion) is exact on the category of finitely generated R-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses inverse-limits exactness (22.6) and Artin–Rees to ensure filtrations are a-stable, so lim← applied to short exact sequences yields exactness after completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completed tensor equals module completion (Corollary 22.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Noetherian R, ideal a, and finitely generated M, the natural map bR ⊗_R M → cM is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from exactness of completion (22.14) and basic tensor-hom adjunctions (8.16). Practical consequence: completion commutes with finite tensoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations among completed ideals and powers (Corollary 22.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) (bM)^ = b cM = b b cM. (2) (b^n)^ = b^n bR = (b bR)^n = (b̂)^n for any n ≥ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use functoriality of completion, injectivity of certain maps, and equalities like bR ⊗ M ≅ cM; useful when comparing completed ideals and their powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of Noetherian ring is flat (Corollary 22.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Noetherian and a an ideal then bR is flat over R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text states 'bR is (cid:13)at' (flat) and uses the Ideal Criterion (9.20) together with previous corollaries about ideals to establish flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered map graded-injective/surjective implies completed map injective/surjective (Lemma 22.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ: M → N is a map of filtered modules (preserving filtrations) and the induced graded map G(φ) is injective (resp. surjective), then the induced map on completions bφ is injective (resp. surjective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses short exact sequences on graded pieces, Snake Lemma, and passage to inverse limits; a technique for lifting information from associated-graded to completions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation of graded module yields finite generation and completeness (Lemma 22.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is complete, M is separated, and G(M) is finitely generated over G(R), then M is finitely generated over R and is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct lifts of generators in G(M) to M, obtain surjective map R^n → M whose completion is surjective by Lemma 22.22, and use separatedness/completeness to conclude M ≅ image and is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete Noetherian graded module yields Noetherian module (Proposition 22.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is complete and M is separated, and G(M) is a Noetherian G(R)-module, then M is a complete Noetherian R-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any submodule N, G(N) is finitely generated so N is finitely generated and complete by Lemma 22.23, hence M is Noetherian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of Noetherian ring is Noetherian (Theorem 22.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Noetherian and a an ideal, then the completion bR is Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: G(R) is finitely generated as R/a-algebra (20.12), so G(R) is Noetherian (Hilbert Basis Theorem); G(bR)=G(R) by (22.9) so bR Noetherian by Proposition 22.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal mapping property of formal power series (Theorem 22.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a ring, R' an R-algebra with ideal b and elements x1,...,xn ∈ b. If R' is separated and complete, there is a unique R-algebra map φ: R[[X1,...,Xn]] → R' sending Xi ↦ xi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct maps to R'/b^m using polynomial maps and take inverse limit; the UMP is the completion analogue of polynomial UMP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen Structure Theorem for complete Noetherian local rings (Theorem 22.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a complete Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m and A contains a coefficient field k (i.e., k ↪ A/m), then A ≅ k[[X1,...,Xn]]/a for some n and ideal a. Further, if A is regular of dimension r, then A ≅ k[[X1,...,Xr]].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: lift generators of m to power series ring via UMP (22.29), show graded map is surjective and use Lemma 22.22 to conclude surjectivity of the map; regular case uses equality of graded rings to conclude kernel trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and basic properties of discrete valuation and DVR (23.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A discrete valuation v: K^× → Z is a surjective homomorphism satisfying v(x+y) ≥ min{v(x),v(y)} for x ≠ −y. The DVR A associated is {x ∈ K | v(x) ≥ 0} ∪ {0}. Properties: A is a local PID/UFD of dimension 1, maximal ideal m = ⟨t⟩ for t with v(t)=1 (uniformizer), every x ∈ K factors uniquely as u t^n with u a unit and n ∈ Z, and nonzero ideals are principal ⟨t^m⟩.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: k[[t]] inside k((t)) and Z_{(p)} with p-adic valuation. Use to characterize regularity/dimension 1 domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: principal maximal ideal and Krull intersection implies DVR (Lemma 23.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a local domain with nonzero principal maximal ideal m = ⟨t⟩ and ⋂_{n≥0} m^n = 0, then A is a DVR (one constructs valuation v by exponents of t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Construct v(x) as exponent n such that x ∈ m^n 
eq m^{n+1}; check valuation axioms and conclude A is the DVR of v.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and M-sequences (Definition 23.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For module M and elements x1,...,xn, the sequence is regular on M (an M-sequence) if Mn ≠ 0 and each xi is not a zerodivisor on Mi−1; depth(a;M) is supremum of lengths of M-sequences in ideal a; for local M depth(M) = depth(rad(M);M). If depth(M)=dim(M), M is Cohen–Macaulay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to measure nonzerodivisors in modules and plays into Serre's conditions and characterizations of Cohen–Macaulay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations and inequalities involving depth (Lemma 23.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) depth(M)=0 iff m ∈ Ass(M). (2) depth(M)=1 iff there exists x ∈ m nonzerodivisor on M and m ∈ Ass(M/xM). (3) depth(M) ≤ dim(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use definitions of associated primes and behavior of dimensions under regular sequences (21.5). Useful for detecting depth in local Noetherian modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for DVR (Theorem 23.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian local ring A with maximal ideal m, the following are equivalent: (1) A is a DVR. (2) A is a normal domain of dimension 1. (3) A is a normal domain of depth 1. (4) A is a regular local ring of dimension 1. (5) m is principal and of height ≥ 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implications shown via UFD/normality, associated primes, Krull intersection theorem, and Lemma 23.3; this provides multiple practical tests to determine whether a 1-dimensional local Noetherian domain is a DVR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization: DVR ↔ nonsingularity of a plane curve at a point (Exercise 23.11 / Example)
rubrics_metrics.description: For P = k[X,Y] and f irreducible with R = P/⟨f⟩ and p = ⟨X,Y⟩/⟨f⟩, the localization R_p is a DVR iff the linear part ℓ(X,Y) of f at the point is nonzero (i.e., the plane curve f=0 is nonsingular at (0,0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates algebraic condition of being a DVR to geometric nonsingularity; useful diagnostic in algebraic geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's conditions Rn and Sn (23.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Noetherian ring R: (R_n) means for any prime p of height m ≤ n, R_p is regular of dimension m. (S_n) means for any prime p of height m, depth(R_p) ≥ min{m,n}. Equivalently, (S_n) says Rp is Cohen–Macaulay when depth(Rp) < n. In particular, (R_1) holds iff (R_0) and R_p is a DVR for any height-1 prime p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are local conditions that together characterize normality when combined appropriately (see Serre's criterion). Useful for checking normality through local checks at low-height primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection of height-1 localizations and normality (Lemmas 23.16, 23.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian domain R let Δ = {p prime | ht(p) = 1} and Σ = {p prime | depth(R_p) = 1}. Then Δ ⊆ Σ, and Δ = Σ iff (S2) holds. Moreover, R = ⋂_{p ∈ Σ} R_p. If R is normal then R = ⋂_{p ∈ Δ} R_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lemmas reduce global membership in R to membership in discrete-valuation-localizations at height-1 primes (or primes of depth 1); foundational for divisor-class-group and normalization arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre's Criterion for normality (Theorem 23.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian domain R is normal iff it satisfies (R1) and (S2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: normal ⇒ localizations are normal so (R1),(S2) hold; conversely, if (R1),(S2) hold then integrally closed elements lie in all height-1 localizations hence in R by the intersection lemma (23.16). This is a standard practical test for normality.
